abilities.name: Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils
_curatorNotes: ⚓ The flask (2026-11-27, Nate: model the fill and the re-press exit, no attack exit; gcsim 41bfe4915 jahoda/skill.go). The press enters Shadow Pursuit at skillWindup = 30f for up to shadowPursuitMaxDuration = 334f, so `duration` 6.07 (364f) is the longest stance. `endsOnFill` (sim/stanceFill.ts): fillFlask polls from 30 + 7 = 37f every 30f, P > H > E > C with the locked element first, +20 for the locked element and +10 for another, max 100; a full flask drains drainFlaskHitmark = 4f later, ending the stance. A steady aura fills it at 157f and drains at 161f.

The drain is the cast's one hit: Filled Treasure Flask at fillHitmark = 2f after a full drain, Unfilled Treasure Flask at unfillHitmark = 4f after the stance's own end or the re-press. Both Anemo, Durability 25, ICDTagElementalArt, one per cast. The drain reads the flask at its instant, as gcsim's drainFlask does. The dash's Smoke Bomb (no contact) is not modelled; gcsim has none.

Frames: skillFrames = InitAbilSlice(12 + 30 = 42), so the re-press is 42f after the press. Every other action waits for the drain: gcsim's Frames func returns (F − src) + skillCancelFrames[next] while the stance runs, then pursuitDuration + skillCancelFrames[next], so the next action starts skillCancelFrames[next] after the drain. That slice is `afterEnd` (Aim → C); the re-press sibling carries the same slice from its press.

Cooldown: cancelPursuit calls SetCD(skill, skillCD + skillWindup) = (15 + 0.5) × 60 = 930f at the drain, so `cooldownStartsAtStanceEnd` with 15.5. The 15.5 against genshin-db's 15 is gcsim's windup term, recorded in GDB_CD_KNOWN_WRONG.
↻ 2026-09-15: gcsim main has her (#2538, frames doc fixed in #2770); FrameMaps and application[] re-migrated against ac2d76dde.
abilities.description:
Jahoda dashes toward her opponent, entering the Shadow Pursuit state upon contact. While in this state, Jahoda moves continuously and swiftly: If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo, she will quietly convert her **Purr-loined Treasure Flask** to that element, gradually filling it. When the duration ends or the skill is used again, Jahoda drains the Purr-loined Treasure Flask and deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a more powerful instance of Anemo DMG.
If her dash fails to make contact with an opponent, Jahoda instead drops a Smoke Bomb at her location, dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents.

Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. When a Fluffy Meowball hits an opponent, Jahoda regenerates 2 Elemental Energy. This effect can be triggered once every 3.5s.

_curatorNotes: Fluffy Meowballs, Ascendant Gleam only (gcsim 41bfe4915 jahoda/skill.go drainFlask/meowballTick): a full flask under Gleam fires one every meowballHitmarkInterval = 116f from firstMeowballFirstHitmark = 129f after the drain, each spending 10 of the flask's 100 points, so ten. Each lands `travel` = 13f after it fires (gcsim's default). Element = flaskAbsorb, the first element the flask locked; Durability 25, ICDTagNone. meowball[9] = 2.432 → 243.2% ATK. The summon lives 129 + 9 × 116 = 1173f (19.55s), the last fire; the next press ends it (gcsim Skill deletes meowballKey). Not modelled: the 2 Energy per hit (3.5s ICD), C1's bounce.

abilities.name: End Shadow Pursuit
_curatorNotes: The E re-press inside Shadow Pursuit (gcsim skill.go Skill, StatusIsActive(shadowPursuitKey)): drainFlask at the press, so the stance ends here and the flask's drain hit (the stance's, `endsOnFill.drain`) lands 4f later. Frames are skillCancelFrames. No hit of its own, no cooldown of its own: the skill's clock starts at this end.

abilities.name: Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter

_curatorNotes: Robot DMG, Ascendant Gleam only (Jahoda round, 2026-11-27; gcsim 41bfe4915 jahoda/burst.go absorbCheckTask/robotAtkTick): each robot polls the aura on its OWN clock, first at 6f + 41f per robot, then every ⌊interval ÷ 3⌋ (46f; 42f under A1 Cryo), P > H > E > C, until the burst ends (790f). On its lock it fires 41f later and every 140f (126f under A1 Cryo, 140 × 0.9) while the burst lasts. 25 durability (1U), ICDTagElementalBurst<El> on ICDGroupJahodaBurst (900f, every 4th, the list's five 1s = cap 5), so robots on one element share a window and robots on two elements do not (`icdPerElement`). FlatDmg burstSkill[9] = 0.310795 → 31.08% ATK. Hits the 3 closest enemies; one target here. Not modelled: A1 Pyro's ×1.3 DMG (a damage figure), C4's +4 Energy per lock.
Robot 1 under A1 Cryo (126f, polls every 42f); first poll 6f. See robot 1's note.
Robot 2; first poll 47f. See robot 1's note.
Robot 2 under A1 Cryo (126f, polls every 42f); first poll 47f. See robot 1's note.
Robot 3, present when A1 (or C2) picks Electro; first poll 88f. See robot 1's note.
Robot 3 under A1 Cryo (126f, polls every 42f), present when A1 (or C2) picks Electro; first poll 88f. See robot 1's note.
Initial burst hit at hitmark=0f (immediately): 259.0% ATK Anemo elemental burst.

Robots: 2 robots base (+1 with A1 Electro), heal active char every 1.45s (87f) for burstHealFlat + burstHealPP×ATK = 1101.7 + 143.77% ATK at lvl=10. Heal authored with both `scaling: 143.77` (ATK%) and `flat: 1101.7` (talent-table flat addend) — 2026-05-09 Quick Schema Wins.
Duration: burstDuration=790f = 13.17s. Authored on summons[].duration. Robots follow active char (combat.Player() targeted in robotAtkTick).
Burst frames: burstFrames=InitAbilSlice(48), ActionSkill=53 ActionAim=55 ActionDash/Jump=54 ActionWalk=55 ActionSwap=36. Per Q-spec swap/N/E/D/J — N defaults to animLen=48.
Cooldown: SetCDWithDelay(burst, 18*60, 1). ConsumeEnergy(13) drains 13 energy from teammates; not modelled.

A4 Sweet Berry Bounty (heal-on-active-with-HP>70% triggers +100 EM 6s on healed char): not authored as Effect — gating on heal-trigger + HP-state-of-target is two layers we don't track. Schema doesn't currently route heal events through Effect triggers.
C1 (50% Meowball bounce): RNG damage extension; not authored.

C6 (Moonsign Gleam: when flask full, +5% CR / +40% CD to all Moonsign party for 20s): caveated on the C6 node below — the originally-authored buffs were removed because the flask-full trigger sits inside the deferred flask system (stale cross-reference corrected, capability sweep 2026-07-28).

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — The robots' summon-lane row and its tick marks. `computeSummonTicks` accepts every `summonTick` effect, so the lane draws marks at the 1.45s HEAL cadence and only that — a Moonsign player sees one evenly-spaced series where the game runs a second ~2.33s damage series that would carry its own marks and its own aura applications. The caveat is anchored to exactly that row ("Only the robots' healing is shown") and warns the reader not to read the visible cadence as the robots' full output. Category: expected-but-absent.

passives.name: Plan to Get Paid
_curatorNotes: A1: Robot enhancement based on highest-count team element (Pyro: +30% robot DMG, Hydro: +20% heal, Electro: +1 robot count, Cryo: -10% interval). Determined at Init time from team composition. With C2 + Moonsign Gleam, also applies the second-highest element's enhancement (up to 2 active).

Authored 2026-11-27 (Jahoda round) as conditions on the robots' damage series: `teamElementRank` rank 1 (gcsim asc.go a1Init: strictly most members, ties by P > H > E > C, none counted → nothing). Electro adds robot 3 (first poll 88f); Cryo is the 126f cadence with 42f polls, authored as each robot's series twice under mutually exclusive conditions. Pyro (×1.3 robot DMG) and Hydro (×1.2 heal) change a figure, not a frame, so they are not authored. gcsim healInterval is a constant 87f, so the heal markers are right under every branch.
passives.description:
When your team has at least one Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo character, the **Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots** from the Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter will be enhanced based on the number of characters of each corresponding element.
Jahoda secretly keeps track of these characters. Among them, the element with the highest number of characters determines the enhancement effect:
· Pyro: Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots deal 130% of their original DMG.
· Hydro: Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots heal for 120% of their original healing amount.
· Electro: The number of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots increases by one.
· Cryo: The attack interval of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots is reduced by 10%.

If there's a tie between elements, the order of priority that determines which enhancement takes effect is: Pyro, Hydro, Electro, then Cryo. Only one elemental effect can initially be triggered.

passives.name: Sweet Berry Bounty
passives.caveat: When a robot’s heal lands on a character above 70% HP, that character also gains 100 EM for 6s — this boost isn’t shown on the timeline.
_curatorNotes: A4: When a Robot heal triggers on active char with HP > 70%, +100 EM to that char for 6s. Three deferred primitives: (1) per-heal-event trigger; (2) HP-state condition on target; (3) the 'lowest HP off-field char' additional heal that the same A4 mechanic also fires. Not authored. The original stub had a self+manual buff effect — removed; replaced with description-only entry.

Caveated (capability sweep 2026-07-28): still unmodelable — the trigger is a heal EVENT from the burst's summon (no heal-event trigger primitive; summonTick effects can't be conditioned on 'a heal landed'), and the 70% gate is on the HEALED target's HP while selfHpAbove/Below gate on the holder (only recipientHpBelow exists, no Above). Jahoda absent from the local gcsim checkout; kit text is the source. (Frames/application provenance moved to the skill and burst notes 2026-09-17.)

constellations.description: When a Fluffy Meowball fired by the **Purr-loined Treasure Flask** from the Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils hits an enemy, there is a 50% chance for it to bounce, dealing the corresponding Elemental DMG to nearby opponents.

notModeled.reason: This bounce happens on a 50% chance. The Rotation Planner doesn’t simulate chance, so the same rotation always draws the same bars for everyone.
